threat_assessment:
The threat calculus changed the day stack 006 passed. At a tier-4 table this is no longer a hug deck that grinds until the punishers win — it is a deck that can present a four-piece, one-turn table-kill, and you must assume every experienced opponent knows it. Your paper signal got louder too: NINE Game Changers now force the bracket-4 floor (Drannith Magistrate joined the eight), and the read hierarchy at a professional table is exact. Rhystic Study on turn 2 is priced in — groans, not removal. Smothering Tithe still gets answered on sight. But the new top of the list is Aetherflux Reservoir next to Hullbreaker Horror: anyone who has done the reading does stack 006's math on sight — mana-neutral loop, triangular life gain, three 50-point activations, dead table — and the pod's every removal spell and counter turns toward you that instant. So the Reservoir is a sandbag card by default. Sol Ring and Arcane Signet are furniture; Hullbreaker reads as a flash fatty and soft counterspell; none of the three telegraphs the kill. The Reservoir does, which means it is the LAST piece you deploy — on the commit turn itself, not a turn early to 'develop.' Telegraph it deliberately in exactly one situation: when the punisher clock is already public (stack 003's upkeep arithmetic on board) and you hold free counters — then a visible Reservoir soaks the artifact removal that would otherwise dismantle Iron Maiden or the Mine layer, and the archenemy mantle freezes a table whose upkeeps are bleeding (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection, strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). That is embracing the threat on your terms; every other early Reservoir is donating information.

The commit turn is now the deck's central play skill, and the sequencing rule is strict: Grand Abolisher is cast ON the commit turn, as its first spell — not the turn before. (The strategic frame allows 'Abolisher the turn before'; disagree at this tier. A telegraphed Abolisher sitting through a full rotation is both removal bait and an announcement — a professional table reads it as 'the combo is next turn' and answers it, or you, at sorcery speed with three players' worth of resources.) Cast first on the go turn, it does triple duty: its static closes every priority window for the rest of your turn; it is cast #1 toward the ledger, because Aetherflux counts every spell you've cast this turn — your setup spells are already storm count; and the only interactable moment left is the response window to Abolisher itself, while the expensive pieces are still safe in hand. Be honest about the windows, because stack 006 is: without Abolisher, all 15 casts and all three activations pass priority to every opponent, activating is not casting so Hullbreaker never triggers in those windows, and the sorcery-speed loop pieces give you zero mid-stack plays. What actually punishes you there is instant-speed only — a counterspell on a loop rock, artifact removal on any piece mid-ledger, a protection effect on the seat you targeted, and above all a damage-redirect effect on an activation: the verified ledger has you at 3 life after the first payment, so a Deflecting Swat-class response kills YOU with your own Reservoir. Under Abolisher the residual outs shrink to land-channel effects — Otawara and Boseiju are land cards, outside 'artifacts, creatures, or enchantments' — and to the interrupts that never needed a window at all: cast-limit and cast-tax statics already on the battlefield. A Rule of Law-class effect ends a 15-cast line outright; a Thalia- or Trinisphere-class tax breaks the loop's verified mana-neutrality (stacks 004/005). Scan the table for those BEFORE you go; they beat Abolisher because they are not responses (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math, strategy:pivot-point).

Drannith Magistrate carries its own political mass — it is the ninth Game Changer and the table treats it that way. Cast turn 2 into a fresh pod it unites three commander-dependent players against you for no immediate return; cast when one commander is the table's shared problem, it is coalition glue that two opponents will actively protect (strategy:multiplayer.politics). Treat it as both a magnet and a bargaining chip, and know its stranding ceiling (Drannith plus Verdict or Path locking a commander out of the zone-replacement recast) is still an unverified candidate — do not promise the table, or yourself, a line no stack has passed. The walker layer changes your flip-point math in the long game: Jace Beleren, Jace, Wielder of Mysteries, and Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim all survive Supreme Verdict in BOTH directions — you can wrath a hostile board while your draw engines keep ticking (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math), and Beleren's +2 reads as a gift while feeding Heliod's discount and the punisher thresholds off all three opponents' draws. Your flip points, updated: (1) engine plus punisher both visible — the stack 003 clock is public, and it now assembles by turn 6 in 41.3% of games (56.5% ever, mean turn 4.154); (2) Forced Fruition resolving — still the loudest card in the deck; (3) Heliod flipped with cards in hand — your untapped mana is read as interaction forever after (commander lands turn 4.144 on average, 89.8% by turn 6); (4) NEW and loudest: Reservoir next to Hullbreaker. The rebuild also fixed v2's honest weakness — closing speed: wincon access is now 50.1% by turn 6 and 61.2% ever (Jace, Wielder of Mysteries counts as a standing wincon), so 'stay small, stay boring' has an expiry date. When the four pieces line up behind an Abolisher, stop playing fair (strategy:pivot-point).
matchups:
Sweeper control / the control mirror: someone must be the beatdown and it still is not you — the stack 003 punisher clock advances while both of you draw-go, so you own the long game (strategy:whos-the-beatdown, strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). V3 made your board sweep-layered on purpose: the three planeswalkers live through every Supreme Verdict, including YOURS — wrath their Torrential Gearhulk board through open permission (it can't be countered) while Beleren and Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim keep drawing; that is resilience bought instead of restraint (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). Creature wraths still hit almost nothing of yours (mean 1.502 bodies by turn 6 in goldfish) — with one big exception: Hullbreaker Horror. It is a combo piece first and a blocker never; do not flash it in early as value into a control seat, because a wrath that takes it costs you the verified kill, not a 7-drop. Your real exposure remains Farewell-class artifact/enchantment mass removal taking the Mine layer, the punishers, and the Reservoir in one card — deploy in layers, never present both punishers plus the Reservoir to one board state, and keep the kill pieces in hand until the commit turn (strategy:pivot-point). Loran of the Third Path plus a Displacer Kitten blink is still your repeatable answer posture, and the Kitten ledger stays honest: stack 005 refuted the mana-positive version — the loop is exactly mana-neutral with a one-time 3-mana exit.

Stax/tax: taxes attack your velocity math — many cheap spells per turn — so recount the hand under the tax before sequencing (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial). Two new facts sharpen this matchup. First, the kill's requirements are brutally small — the four pieces and {2} to start (stack 006) — so you RACE soft locks that don't touch artifact casts; but cast-limit and cast-tax pieces beat the line structurally, not interactively: Rule of Law-class effects cap a 15-cast turn dead, and a per-spell tax breaks the 004-verified mana-neutrality, so against those your role flips to beatdown on the lock itself — answer the compounding second piece, not the first inconvenience (a lone Thalia is an annoyance; Thalia plus Deafening Silence is a funeral). Second, you are now partly the denial player: Drannith Magistrate shuts off every opponent's commander and every non-hand cast, which in commander-dependent pods makes YOU the lock. Heliod's per-opponent-draw discount remains the tax rebate no other deck gets — Kwain activations and The Second Doctor's end-step gifts keep growing it even under a Sphere — and Kitten-blinking Loran is repeatable lock-piece removal.

Aggro: Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, and The Second Doctor's rider are virtual card advantage tripled at a four-player table (strategy:card-advantage.virtual); commit nothing, hold Supreme Verdict, and let them overextend into the uncounterable reset (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). The Fruition trap still has a name: never lead Forced Fruition into an aggro pod — sequence Iron Maiden or Ebony Owl Netsuke first so the seven-card refill arrives taxed (stack 003: hands over seven pay on upkeep, cleanup trims to exactly seven, damage lands before the cards are spent). V3 adds a life-ledger caveat this matchup owns: the Reservoir kill pays 50 life three times, and stack 006's 15-cast minimum is computed FROM 32 LIFE. The arithmetic generalizes (k(k+1)/2 ≥ 151 minus your life total): at 20 life the minimum is 16 casts, at 8 life it is 17 — each extra cast is another open priority window, so every point of chip damage you absorb is combo disruption whether the aggro player knows it or not. Against aggro, your life total is a combo resource: pillow hard, let Kwain and the Reservoir's own setup-cast triggers pad the ledger, and go a turn earlier rather than a window longer.

Combo and storm: still the discipline test, but v3 flipped the polarity. The free suite — Fierce Guardianship, Force of Negation, Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Dovin's Veto — is held by turn 6 in 62% of goldfish games (73.3% ever); spend it only on the card that ends the game, per the answer-economy bar (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). Drannith Magistrate blanks commander-centric and non-hand lines before they start — flashback, escape, and cast-from-exile engines all die to 'from anywhere other than their hands' — so land it EARLY against a known combo seat and let it eat a removal spell that was earmarked for your win. And with a verified 15-cast kill behind Grand Abolisher's closed windows against wincon access in 50.1% of games by turn 6, you are now frequently the faster, better-protected combo deck in the pod — which flips your role to beatdown, and the racer does not durdle (strategy:whos-the-beatdown, strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). The standing warning survives every version: the hug layer is a liability here. Kwain stays untapped, The Second Doctor's offer goes to the other two seats, and Forced Fruition stays in hand against spellslinger unless a punisher is down and you are the one about to win.

Graveyard decks and incidental hate: your own graveyard needs are still trivial — Dig Through Time's delve and Torrential Gearhulk's flashback target — so an opposing Rest in Peace costs you a card's worth of value, not a plan, and it never touches the Hullbreaker kill. Against the graveyard seat, v3 gave you a real card: Drannith stops every CAST from a graveyard (flashback, escape, disturb), though not reanimation — Reanimate-style effects put the creature onto the battlefield without casting it, and Drannith's text only polices casting. Know that distinction before you tap out trusting it: against cast-based recursion Drannith is a lock piece; against true reanimator your answers are still the counterspell suite and Path/Swords on the body, and that seat meets the free-counter bar early and often.
how_it_wins:
This deck hands the whole table a firehose of cards, then charges for the water. The engines — Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Temple Bell, Dictate of Kruphix, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Folio of Fancies, and above all Forced Fruition — are perfectly symmetric on their face, and the hug layer leans into it: Kwain offers everyone a card (and a life), The Second Doctor offers another at your end step. Heliod is the hinge that makes all of it asymmetric: the front face rebuys an enchantment on arrival, and the {3}{U/P} flip into the Warped Eclipse grants everything flash and discounts your spells {1} for each card your opponents drew this turn — every card the table accepts pays your mana bill on the turn you want to act. The goldfish sim has Heliod down by turn 6 in 89.8% of games (median turn 4), and while the pieces gather you play draw-go control behind a counter suite held by turn 6 in 62% of games, with Supreme Verdict as the uncounterable reset your own planeswalkers now survive.

The primary win is verified end to end, and it is a storm kill: Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + Arcane Signet + Aetherflux Reservoir (stack 006, checker-passed). The 004-verified loop — each rock's cast bounces the other, tapped for its mana before it leaves — is exactly mana-neutral, so casts are unbounded in one main phase, and the Reservoir converts the count into life: cast n nets +n, so k casts pay out k(k+1)/2. From 32 life you need that sum to reach 119, which makes 15 casts the proven minimum (14 casts pay only 105 and fail). The verified schedule: casts 1–6 lift you to 53, the first 'Pay 50 life: 50 damage' activation drops you to 3 and kills the 26-life opponent via state-based actions; casts 7–12 rebuild to 60, the second activation (60 to 10) kills the 40-life seat; casts 13–15 reach 52, the third (52 to 2) kills the last, and with every opponent gone you win on the spot — all in one main phase, ending at 2 life. The same artifact names the line's weakness honestly: every activation (and every loop cast) opens a fully open priority window. Activating an ability is not casting a spell, so Hullbreaker never triggers on it, and the loop's sorcery-speed artifact pieces can only be cast with the stack empty — the engine cannot respond to anything, ever. Grand Abolisher, now maindeck, is the named answer: during your turn opponents can't cast spells or activate artifact, creature, or enchantment abilities, closing exactly the windows the kill opens. Win-condition access is drawn by turn 6 in 50.1% of goldfish runs — up from 42.6% — and the whole line needs {2} and the pieces, nothing more.

The second verified path is the clean one: Approach of the Second Sun. The first cast gains 7 life — 14 with Alhammarret's Archive out — and buries the card seventh from the top, trivially shallow when everyone draws in bulk and two doublers accelerate your digging; Mystical Tutor or Long-Term Plans puts it back on top directly. Stack 002 verified the second cast end to end: the win is checked during resolution, as a spell effect, and the first casting still counts because the game tracks the casting event, not the shuffled-away card. The opponents' one and only window is while the second Approach sits on the stack — commit behind held countermagic, because once resolution begins, nothing stops it.

The third verified path is attrition: the punisher clock. Iron Maiden and Viseling deal upkeep damage equal to hand size minus 4, and Ebony Owl Netsuke deals a flat 4 at seven-plus cards. Stack 003 verified the arithmetic: once Forced Fruition fills a hand, cleanup trims the opponent to exactly 7, and the next upkeep Owl hits for 4 and Maiden for 3 — 7 damage without you tapping a land, running on all three opponents' upkeeps. The Second Doctor makes 7 the floor, not the ceiling: with no maximum hand size the trim never happens, so a ten-card hand takes 6 from the Maiden while the Owl keeps firing. The core two-piece — engine plus punisher — assembles by turn 6 in 41.3% of games, so most games open as pure control; the deck is built to be good at exactly that, and the moment the four kill pieces line up behind an Abolisher, you stop playing fair.

combo_lines.001: What this deck does NOT do. The combo database lists Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring as a two-card infinite (296,000 decks believe it); this walk refutes it. The Horror's trigger is modal, and mode and target lock in while the Sol Ring that caused it is still a spell on the stack — a spell you control is not a legal target for 'target spell you don't control,' and it is not a nonland permanent either. By the time Sol Ring is a permanent, the trigger is gone. The pair alone loops nothing: no mana, no storm count. Never pitch this deck to the table — or compute its bracket — on the strength of that database line.
combo_lines.002: The second Approach of the Second Sun, put on top by Mystical Tutor and cast from your hand. The two questions that decide games: yes, the first casting still counts even though the card was shuffled back into your library — the condition checks an event in the game's history, not the card object — and the win is checked mid-resolution, as a spell effect, not a state-based action. The opponents' one and only window is while Approach sits on the stack; the walk plays out the counter-war, including Swan Song answering their counterspell with {U} held. Once all players pass and resolution begins, the game simply ends.
combo_lines.003: The punisher core doing its job under fire. An opponent tries to Naturalize Forced Fruition — and the Fruition trigger sits on top of the very spell that caused it, so they draw their seven cards before the enchantment dies (and the ability would survive its source's destruction anyway). Cleanup trims them to exactly 7 in hand, which is precisely the threshold both punishers want: next upkeep, Ebony Owl Netsuke's intervening-if sees seven cards and deals 4, Iron Maiden deals 7 minus 4 = 3, for 7 total. Both triggers are yours, so you order them — though here neither changes hand size, so the math is order-proof.
combo_lines.004: The real Hullbreaker engine — three cards, not two. Cast the two-mana rock; the Horror's trigger targets Sol Ring, which IS a legal target because it's on the battlefield, a permanent, not a spell. Tap Sol Ring for {C}{C} while the trigger is on the stack (a mana ability — nothing can respond), let the bounce resolve, recast Sol Ring, bounce and tap the Signet in turn. One full cycle: 3 mana spent, 3 produced — exactly mana-neutral, so the cast count is unbounded within one main phase off a {2} investment. It nets no mana, cards, or damage by itself, and aiming a trigger at an opponent's permanent breaks the chain. Thought Vessel substitutes for Arcane Signet exactly; Fellwar Stone only while an opponent's land can actually produce mana.
combo_lines.005: What the Kitten does NOT do to the engine. The hope: Displacer Kitten blinks Sol Ring untapped mid-loop, and stack 004's mana-neutral cycle goes mana-positive. This walk refutes it. Both of your triggers lock their targets at announcement, and whichever resolves first turns the shared useful target into a new object — so the second trigger's target is illegal and it fizzles. Horror's bounce and the Kitten's blink are mutually exclusive on every cast. Keep the loop alive and the Kitten contributes exactly nothing: the cycle stays exactly 3 spent, 3 produced. Blink first and you really do tap Sol Ring twice on that cast — but Horror's bounce fizzles, your hand empties, and the loop TERMINATES: a one-time exit worth 3 floating mana against the best Kitten-less exit's 2. Unbounded casts survive untouched; unbounded mana does not exist, and an X spell off this engine is capped at that terminal float of at most 3.
combo_lines.006: The verified table-kill, and the reason this deck's bracket-4 floor is honest: Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + Arcane Signet + Aetherflux Reservoir, checker-passed end to end with an exact ledger. The 004-verified loop supplies unbounded casts; the Reservoir converts them — cast n nets +n life, so k casts pay k(k+1)/2, and from 32 life you need at least 119, making 15 casts the proven minimum (14 pays 105 and falls short). The walk interleaves three 'Pay 50 life' activations at the only legal points: 53 to 3 (first kill), 60 to 10 (second), 52 to 2 (third), each 50 damage killing its target via state-based actions, all in one main phase, you alive at 2. The verified weakness comes with it: every activation opens a fully open priority window — activating is not casting, so Hullbreaker never triggers on it, and the sorcery-speed loop pieces can't be cast in response to anything. Grand Abolisher, now maindeck, is the named answer: on your turn it closes every one of those windows.

card_roles.Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the: Front face: a 4/4 that returns a non-God enchantment from your graveyard on arrival — Forced Fruition or Rhystic Study back after a wrath is the usual pick. The {3}{U/P} flip (sorcery speed, payable with 2 life) turns on the deck: the Warped Eclipse grants all your spells flash and discounts them {1} per card your opponents drew this turn — your own table-draw engines, Kwain activations, and Second Doctor end-step gifts pay your costs while you keep mana up for counters.
card_roles.Forced Fruition: The punisher core's detonator: every opponent spell is seven forced draws, feeding Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke, and Viseling past their thresholds instantly. Stack 003 verified the trigger resolves even when the spell it triggered on is the removal that kills it.
card_roles.Iron Maiden: Hand-size-minus-4 damage at each opponent's upkeep, computed on resolution. Inert against a five-card hand; a three-a-turn clock once the engines are running — and with The Second Doctor removing the cleanup trim, the count climbs past stack 003's floor of 3.
card_roles.Ebony Owl Netsuke: A flat 4 at each opponent's upkeep at seven-plus cards — the intervening-if is checked both at trigger and on resolution. With Iron Maiden, exactly 7 damage per punished upkeep off a cleanup-trimmed hand (stack 003); with The Second Doctor keeping hands untrimmed, the check just keeps passing.
card_roles.Viseling: Iron Maiden with a body — same hand-minus-4 upkeep damage on a 1/1 construct. Redundancy for the deck's core clock; dies to creature removal (and your own Supreme Verdict) where the Maiden doesn't.
card_roles.Kwain, Itinerant Meddler: The political engine, new in this build: {T} lets each player draw, and drawers gain 1 life. Every card an opponent accepts inches them toward the punisher thresholds and grows Heliod's discount; every card they decline is a card behind. Your side of the tap doubles twice under Alhammarret's Archive — two cards and 2 life — and a two-mana body that makes the whole table like you buys exactly the waiting turns a 39.6%-by-turn-6 two-piece needs.
card_roles.The Second Doctor: 'Players have no maximum hand size' is the quiet punisher enabler: opponents never trim at cleanup, so Ebony Owl's 7+ check keeps passing and Iron Maiden's hand-minus-4 grows unbounded — while you hoard your own doubled draws without needing Reliquary Tower. The end-step rider is a pillow fort on legs: each opponent who accepts the draw can't attack you or your permanents next turn, stacking with Propaganda and Ghostly Prison, and the cards they take feed the Maiden anyway. Heads they can't attack, tails they fall behind.
card_roles.Alhammarret's Archive: The asymmetry hinge for both of the deck's currencies: every draw of yours after the first in your draw step becomes two, and all your lifegain doubles. Kwain's tap pays you double on both halves, the Mine effects become personal Fonts on your side only, a first Approach of the Second Sun banks 14 life instead of 7, and it stacks with Teferi's Ageless Insight as a second your-side draw doubler. Five mana that converts every symmetric engine you run into a rigged one.
card_roles.Supreme Verdict: The uncounterable reset this deck lacked: four mana, destroy all creatures, and the blue player can do nothing about it. Your clock lives in artifacts and enchantments, so the wrath is nearly one-sided — it does take Kwain, Kami, and your other engine bodies, so time it for when the board, not your own value layer, is the problem.
card_roles.Psychosis Crawler: Drains each opponent for 1 per card YOU draw, and its stats track your hand. With the X-draw suite and the doublers it converts a big refill into table-wide reach — a candidate line flagged for stack verification, not yet walked.
card_roles.Scrawling Crawler: A symmetric upkeep draw stapled to an asymmetric tax: each opponent draw costs them a life, so every engine on your board turns it into a slow burn.
card_roles.Sphinx's Tutelage: Turns your own draws into repeated two-card mills with a shared-color cascade — an alternate attrition angle that scales with the draw doublers and the wheels.
card_roles.Howling Mine: The classic symmetric engine: an extra draw at each draw step while untapped. Symmetric on its face; the punishers, the Archive, and Heliod's discount make it yours.
card_roles.Font of Mythos: Howling Mine doubled — two extra draws for everyone. The fastest way to push the table to seven cards, and the biggest per-turn Heliod discount.
card_roles.Temple Bell: A draw for everyone on demand, at instant speed — which means you can ring it on an opponent's upkeep after their draw step to push a hand over the punisher threshold, or in response to removal for pure value.
card_roles.Dictate of Kruphix: The flash Howling Mine — deploy it end of turn, ahead of the opponent whose upkeep you most want taxed.
card_roles.Kami of the Crescent Moon: Howling Mine on legs for two mana. Cheapest engine in the deck; also the most fragile.
card_roles.Folio of Fancies: Three jobs: removes YOUR maximum hand size, force-feeds the table X cards at once, and can mill an opponent for their whole (bloated) hand. The X-draw activation is the precision tool for pushing hands over 7 at the right moment.
card_roles.Rhystic Study: The asymmetric half of the value layer: every opponent spell is a card or a tax, and in a deck this dense with forced action it is a firehose. The Warped Eclipse doesn't discount off it (it counts draws, and Study's draws are yours) — but it wins the card war that decides control mirrors.
card_roles.Mystic Remora: Rhystic Study's early-game twin — a turn-1 Remora often draws three-plus cards before the cumulative upkeep bites. Pay a couple of ages, then let it go — or don't: a Displacer Kitten blink returns it as a new object with no age counters, and the tax restarts from zero.
card_roles.Smothering Tithe: Every opponent draw is {2} or a Treasure for you — and this deck makes opponents draw in sevens. Forced Fruition plus Tithe presents seven pay-or-treasure decisions per opponent spell (flagged for stack verification of the exact yield).
card_roles.Consecrated Sphinx: Two cards to you for every card an opponent draws. Under any table engine this is obscene; under Forced Fruition it is fourteen cards per opponent spell. The single strongest magnet for removal you play.
card_roles.Teferi's Ageless Insight: Doubles every draw of yours past the first each draw step — your Howling Mines become personal Fonts, and digging seven cards to a buried Approach takes half the turns. Stacks with Alhammarret's Archive.
card_roles.Faerie Mastermind: Flash body that pays you a card whenever an opponent draws their second card each turn — free value under your own engines — with an activated Temple Bell stapled on for pushing hands at instant speed.
card_roles.Hullbreaker Horror: The spine of the verified primary win. An uncounterable flash 7/8 whose cast trigger bounces a spell or permanent — a tempo monster in the midgame, and with Sol Ring plus Arcane Signet it is the unbounded, mana-neutral cast loop (stack 004) that Aetherflux Reservoir converts into the table-kill (stack 006). Two verified limits: the two-card 'infinite' with Sol Ring alone is refuted (stack 001), and the Horror gives the kill zero protection — activating the Reservoir is not casting, so its trigger never fires during the windows that matter.
card_roles.Displacer Kitten: Blinks one of your nonland permanents on each noncreature cast — and in a 99 that is mostly noncreature spells, that is constantly. The oracle-grounded payoffs: a blinked Mystic Remora returns as a new object with zero age counters, so the cumulative upkeep resets (the long-run value of that free Remora is still a candidate line, not yet walked); a blinked tapped Sol Ring returns untapped; a blinked Loran or Faerie Mastermind re-triggers and untaps for another activation. One question is now settled, and the answer is no: stack 005 refutes the hope that the Kitten makes the stack-004 loop mana-positive — target lock at announcement plus the new-object rule make its blink and Horror's bounce mutually exclusive on every cast, so the loop stays exactly mana-neutral, and blinking Sol Ring is a one-time, loop-terminating exit worth +1 floating mana.
card_roles.Sol Ring: The best rock in the format and one of the four pieces of the verified kill — the loop taps it for {C}{C} with the bounce trigger already on the stack (stack 004), and every recast adds one to the Reservoir's count (stack 006).
card_roles.Arcane Signet: Fixes into either color and completes the kill engine: its cast bounces Sol Ring, its tap keeps the cycle at exactly 3-in, 3-out (stack 004) — and in stack 006's walk it is cast #1 of the fifteen.
card_roles.Thought Vessel: Two jobs verified or textual: an exact substitute for Arcane Signet in the Hullbreaker loop (same neutral ledger, per stack 004), and no-maximum-hand-size insurance that survives the creature wraths The Second Doctor doesn't.
card_roles.Fellwar Stone: Ramp that reads opponents' lands — and a conditional loop piece: it sustains the 004 engine only while an opponent controls a land that produces mana; on an empty board the cycle goes mana-negative and the loop dies.
card_roles.Fierce Guardianship: Free countermagic while Heliod is out — the card that lets you tap out for an engine piece and still say no. Part of why the sim shows interaction held in 73% of games.
card_roles.Force of Negation: The other free counter: pitch a blue card on an opponent's turn to stop a noncreature spell and exile it. Guards the punisher board through your tapped-out turns.
card_roles.Swan Song: One mana, counters the counterspell aimed at your second Approach — the exact play walked in stack 002. The 2/2 Bird is a bargain against winning the game.
card_roles.An Offer You Can't Refuse: One-mana noncreature counter; the two Treasures you hand over are a real cost, so aim it at spells that matter — sweepers, counters in the Approach war.
card_roles.Dovin's Veto: The argument-ender: can't be countered itself. The premium hold for your commit turn.
card_roles.Counterspell: The unconditional classic. Two blue is easy in a 36-source blue base.
card_roles.Arcane Denial: Counters anything for {1}{U} and replaces itself next upkeep; the two cards it feeds the opponent are, in this deck, more fuel for your punishers.
card_roles.Approach of the Second Sun: The clean second wincon. First cast: 7 life — 14 under Alhammarret's Archive — and seventh from the top, shallow when everyone's drawing in bulk. Second cast from hand wins during resolution, verified end to end in stack 002; the only window to stop it is on the stack. Wincon access sits at 50.1% by turn 6 in the v3 goldfish, so between this and the storm kill the tutors always have a live target.
card_roles.Aetherflux Reservoir: No longer a flagged candidate — the verified kill (stack 006). 'Gain 1 life for each spell you've cast this turn' turns the mana-neutral Hullbreaker loop into triangular life growth (cast n nets +n), and three 'Pay 50 life: 50 damage' activations clear the table in one main phase, 15 casts minimum from 32 life. Remember the verified fine print: the 50 life is paid before anyone can respond, and each activation's window is fully open unless Grand Abolisher is down.
card_roles.Secure the Wastes: Instant-speed X warriors: a board out of nowhere with all your held-up mana at someone's end step, or emergency blockers.
card_roles.Metallurgic Summonings: Constructs sized to each instant or sorcery you cast; the buyback clause returns your whole spell graveyard once you control six artifacts, which this deck reaches without trying.
card_roles.Mystical Tutor: The Approach enabler: end-step tutor puts the second copy on top for the win next turn (stack 002's setup). Also finds Supreme Verdict or the right counterspell on demand — part of why wincon access reached 50.1% by turn 6 in the v3 sim.
card_roles.Long-Term Plans: Any card, third from the top — with your draw density and two doublers that's one turn away. Unlike Mystical Tutor it can fetch permanents: Aetherflux, a punisher, the missing loop rock.
card_roles.Mathemagics: Draws 2^X cards — the most explosive refill in the deck and the scariest thing to point at yourself with Psychosis Crawler out (candidate line, unverified).
card_roles.Prosperity: Symmetric X-draw for the table: pushes every hand toward punisher range at once, on your terms.
card_roles.Skyscribing: Prosperity with a forecast rider — a free-ish draw for everyone each upkeep from your hand, keeping hands topped up without spending the card.
card_roles.Braingeyser: Targeted X-draw: refill yourself, or force-feed one opponent over the Netsuke threshold at sorcery speed.
card_roles.Stroke of Genius: Braingeyser at instant speed — refill on an end step, or push a hand over 7 in response to their upkeep triggers going on the stack.
card_roles.Dig Through Time: Delve makes this two mana in the mid game: seven deep for exactly the two cards you need — usually a counter and a threat, or the buried Approach.
card_roles.Ghostly Prison: Pays for the deck's low creature count: attackers cost {2} each, and the whole table's mana is already stretched by your taxes.
card_roles.Propaganda: Ghostly Prison's blue twin. Two copies of this effect, The Second Doctor's no-attack rider, and punisher upkeep damage make attacking you the worst-value line at the table.
card_roles.Teferi's Protection: The panic button: life locked, everything phases out, you lose nothing to the wrath — and your engine board returns intact before your untap.
card_roles.Cyclonic Rift: The asymmetric reset. Overloaded on an end step it clears every opposing board while your punisher artifacts stay put.
card_roles.Swords to Plowshares: Premium one-mana creature exile; the life you give away comes back as upkeep damage.
card_roles.Path to Exile: The second one-mana exile. The basic land you gift is a real cost — save it for the creature that actually kills you.
card_roles.Loran of the Third Path: Artifact/enchantment removal on a body, plus a tap that draws you and an opponent a card — removal that also feeds the punishers, and the premium Displacer Kitten blink target for a re-triggered Disenchant.
card_roles.Torrential Gearhulk: Flash 5/6 that recasts a counterspell or Dig Through Time from the graveyard for free — a threat that interacts the turn it arrives.
card_roles.Leyline of Anticipation: Flash for everything before Heliod flips (and redundancy after) — free from the opening hand, which is when the deck most wants to play draw-go.
card_roles.Reliquary Tower: No maximum hand size on a land — redundant with The Second Doctor and Thought Vessel now, and the copy that survives every wrath.
card_roles.Mikokoro, Center of the Sea: A Temple Bell on a land: repeatable, uncounterable hand-stuffing that survives every board wipe.
card_roles.Homeward Path: Theft insurance on a land — everyone takes their own creatures back, which against the mind-control and theft decks usually means you take yours back.
card_roles.Grand Abolisher: The kill-turn shield, added for exactly the hole stack 006 verified: every Reservoir activation and every loop cast opens a fully open priority window, Hullbreaker offers no protection (activating isn't casting), and the sorcery-speed pieces can't respond to anything. Abolisher's static — during your turn, opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments — closes every one of those windows. Sequence it the turn before you go, or lead the combo turn with it; two mana buys an uninterruptable 15-cast line.
card_roles.Drannith Magistrate: The ninth Game Changer on the bracket report, and a denial engine in one static: opponents can't cast spells from anywhere but their hands — no commanders from the command zone, no flashback, no foretell, no cascade. In commander-dependent pods you are suddenly the lock. The stranding package with Supreme Verdict or Path (exile the commander, Drannith locks the recast) is a flagged candidate line, not yet stack-verified.
card_roles.Jace Beleren: A Howling Mine that survives Farewell — and your own Supreme Verdict. The +2 hands every player a card, feeding the punisher thresholds and Heliod's discount from three opponents at once while ticking toward more loyalty; the −1 pushes a specific hand over the Netsuke line, or draws you the piece. Three mana for a table engine no wrath in the format's mainstream removal suite touches.
card_roles.Jace, Wielder of Mysteries: A standing wincon in a permanent: 'If you would draw a card while your library has no cards in it, you win the game instead,' with a +1 that draws while it threatens. It's why goldfish wincon access rose to 50.1% by turn 6. The deliberate self-deck win — Archive-doubled X-draws emptying your own library — is a flagged candidate awaiting a stack scenario; the replacement-ordering questions are real, so don't bet the game on it until it's walked.
card_roles.Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim: The planeswalker built for a deck that does nothing but draw: every draw adds loyalty, so under your Mine effects and doublers he charges himself faster than the table can attack him down — and he survives your own Supreme Verdict. The −2 Spirit grows a +1/+1 counter per draw into a real blocker-then-threat, and the −12 is a one-sided board shuffle you actually reach.

mulligan: The v3 sim keeps 73.6% of first sevens and mulligans gently (0.33 per game), so the bar is: two to four lands (the kept-hand distribution centers on 2-3 plus rocks — 18 lands means the nine rocks are load-bearing, and Ancient Tomb plus a two-drop rock is how 28.1% of games cast Heliod by turn 3), one card-flow piece, and something to say 'no' with. What you are actually mulliganing toward is flow plus interaction, not any combo: a table-draw engine is drawn by turn 6 in 75.7% of games (mean turn 2.5) — call it the 76% promise — and cheap or free interaction is held by then in 62% (73.3% of games ever). Those are the reliable axes, and Kwain and Jace Beleren both count among the cheap engines worth keeping a hand for. The full two-piece — engine PLUS punisher — is assembled by turn 6 in only 41.3% of games (56.5% ever, mean turn 4.2), so never keep a marginal hand because it 'promises the lock'; the punishers are inert on their own (Iron Maiden reads hand minus 4 — against a normal hand that's one damage). A hand of two punishers and no draw engine is a mulligan in costume: ship it. The same discipline applies doubly to the verified kill — four specific pieces is not a mulligan target, it's what Long-Term Plans and the 75.7% draw engine find for you in the midgame. And don't dig for wincons at hand-quality prices: access is 50.1% by turn 6 now that Jace, Wielder of Mysteries counts as a standing wincon, and the tutors carry the rest. Heliod himself needs no help — 89.8% of games cast him by turn 6, median turn 4 — so keep hands that use the turns before him: Remora into rock into Kami (or Kwain) is the curve the deck was built to play.
upgrades: Start with the good news: the v3 rebuild already cashed the obsolescence index's two clearest checks — Worn Powerstone (superseded by the two-mana Talisman class) and Brass Infiniscope (flagged for Daily Bugle Newspaper) both left the 99 in this pass, so the index's actionable debt is paid. What remains is nuance, not urgency. Azorius Signet's entry lists Mind Stone among its superseders — 'additional: draw' — a fair swap only if you value the late-game cash-in over colored fixing in a two-color deck. The index flags Fellwar Stone as obsoleted by Sol Ring on cost, but you already run Sol Ring, and Fellwar's real demerit is the verified one: it only sustains the Hullbreaker loop while an opponent's land can actually make mana. Long-Term Plans is indexed as obsoleted by Mystical Tutor, which you also run — but the supersession is narrower than it looks, since Plans fetches any card (a punisher, Aetherflux Reservoir, the missing loop rock) where Mystical only finds instants and sorceries; keep both. Counterspell draws entries for Syncopate and Spell Snare on cost alone — both are conditional counters by their own text, a poor trade in a deck that plans to hold mana anyway. The incoming five were checked too: Grand Abolisher, Drannith Magistrate, Jace Beleren, and Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim have no index entries at all, and Jace, Wielder of Mysteries' lone entry — Jace, the Perfected Mind, 'additional: removal' — fails the oracle-text test on the only clause that matters: the Perfected Mind has no empty-library win static, which is the entire reason Wielder is in this deck. Same verdict as last pass's re-checks (Alhammarret's Archive vs Autograph Book, Supreme Verdict vs Devout Decree, The Second Doctor vs Sokka, Kwain vs the plain looters): similarity artifacts, every one — the clauses you run these cards for have no printed replacement. The standing negative result also holds: the punisher core itself — Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke, Viseling, Howling Mine, Font of Mythos — has no obsolescence entries. Nothing printed since does this job better; the old cards are the tech, not the debt. Outside the index entirely, the deck-analyst gap study on two-piece consistency (41.3% assembled by turn 6) still names the same three outside-pool answers: Enlightened Tutor, a one-mana instant that puts any artifact or enchantment piece of the core on top — every engine and punisher except Kami of the Crescent Moon — at the cost of a tenth Game Changer the bracket-4 floor already absorbs; Fabricate, which fetches any of the artifact pieces straight to hand; and Trouble in Pairs, which converts the second draw your engines guarantee every opponent every turn into cards for you instead of damage. Those three are the consistency ceiling this list hasn't bought yet — deck-analyst shortlist evidence, not obsolescence data, so weigh them as recommendations rather than supersessions.
